IDPs stood near 5 million in early 2025 before falling to roughly 5.8 million-adjusted estimates in 2026 as ~1.9 million returnees were recorded, mostly in North Kivu, South Kivu and Ituri.
Conflict displaced 9.7 million people within the DRC in 2025, the country's highest figure on record and nearly a third of the global total that year.
OCHA projected 14.9 million people would need humanitarian assistance in 2026, with food insecurity affecting 28 million nationwide.

category: Ebola/Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak, since May 15, 2026
note: Deaths passed 3,000 for the first time on Sept 2, 2026 (3,007 deaths/6,186 cases per DRC's INSP); by INSP's Sept 18 data the confirmed toll had risen to 3,639 deaths among 7,541 cases (48.3% case-fatality rate, 1,823 recovered), spread across 62 health zones in seven provinces. An imported case confirmed Sept 10 newly spread the outbreak to Sud-Ubangi, the seventh affected province, covering roughly 240,000 sq km. Ituri remains the epicenter and transmission there is beginning to slow, though ~300 new cases and 160 deaths were still recorded in the week to Sept 18; North Kivu's weekly case count nearly doubled over two weeks. A 20,000-person Ervebo vaccine clinical trial testing efficacy against the Bundibugyo strain began in Bunia, Ituri on Sept 19, 2026. This remains DRC's largest and deadliest Ebola outbreak on record and the second-largest globally. Congolese experts say the true toll could be several times higher than confirmed figures.
